chunks: Sama'ah narrated from Abu Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you raise your head from the second prostration in the first rak'ah, at the time you intend to stand, sit upright, then stand."
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended sitting posture between the prostrations in the first rak'ah of prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies the *qaa'dah* (sitting posture) between the second prostration and standing in the first rak'ah, a detail often discussed in Shia jurisprudence regarding the completeness of the prayer's form. It underscores the meticulous attention to physical etiquette (*adab*) in Shia ritual practice, distinguishing the recommended sitting position from mere transition. This instruction reflects the broader Shia emphasis on replicating the Prophet’s and Imams’ precise movements as transmitted through reliable chains like Sama'ah and Abu Basir.
